The '''Minlos–Sasonov theorem''' is a result from [[measure theory in topological vector spaces]]. It provides a sufficient condition for a [[cylindrical measure]] to be [[Sigma-additive set function|σ-additive]] on a [[locally convex space]]. This is the case when its [[Fourier transform]] is [[Continuous function|continuous]] at [[zero]] in the ''Sazonov topology'' and such a topology is called ''sufficient''. The theorem is named after the two [[Russia|Russian]] mathematicians [[Robert Minlos|Robert Adol'fovich Minlos]] and [[Vyacheslav Vasilievich Sazonov]].

The theorem generalizes two classical theorem: the [[Minlos theorem]] (1963) and the [[Sazonov theorem]] (1958). It was then later generalized in the 1970s by the mathematicians [[Albert Badrikian]] and [[Laurent Schwartz]] to locally convex spaces. Therefore, the theorem is sometimes also called '''Minlos-Sasonov-Badrikian theorem'''.<ref>{{cite book |first=Albert |last=Badrikian |publisher=Springer |title=Séminaire Sur les Fonctions Aléatoires Linéaires et les Mesures Cylindriques |series=Lecture Notes in Math. |volume=139 |date=1970}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |first=Laurent |last=Schwartz |publisher=Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Studies in Mathematics |title=Radon measures on arbitrary topological spaces and cylindrical measures |number=6 |date=1973}}</ref>

==Minlos–Sasonov theorem==
Let <math>(X,\tau)</math> be a [[locally convex space]], <math>X^*</math> and <math>X'</math> are the corresponding algebraic and topological [[dual space]]s, and <math>\langle,\rangle:X\times X'\to \mathbb{R}</math> is the [[Dual system|dual pair]]. A topology <math>\tau^K</math> on <math>X</math> is called ''compatible'' with the dual pair <math>\langle,\rangle</math> if the corresponding topological dual space induced by <math>\tau^K</math> is again <math>X'</math>. A [[seminorm]] <math>p</math> on <math>X</math> is called ''Hilbertian'' or a ''Hilbert seminorm'' if there exists a positive definite [[bilinear form]] <math>b\colon X\times X\to\mathbb{R}</math> such that <math>p(x)=\sqrt{b(x,x)}</math> for all <math>x\in X</math>.

Let <math>\mathfrak{A}:=\mathfrak{A}(X,X'):=\bigotimes\limits_{n=1}^{\infty}\mathfrak{A}_{f_1,\dots,f_n}</math> denote the [[cylindrical σ-algebra|cylindrical algebra]].<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Richard M. |last1=Dudley |first2=Jacob |last2=Feldman |first3=Lucien |last3=Le Cam |publisher=Princeton University |title=On Seminorms and Probabilities, and Abstract Wiener Spaces |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=93 |number=2 |date=1971 |pages=390-392}}</ref> 

===Deriving the Sazonov topology===
Let <math>p</math> be a seminorm on <math>X</math> and <math>X_{p}</math> be the [[factor space]] <math>X_{p}:=X/p^{-1}(0)</math> with canonical mapping <math>Q_{p}:X\to X_{p}</math> defined as <math>Q_{p}:x\mapsto [x]</math>. Let <math>\overline{p}</math> be the [[norm (mathematics)|norm]]
:<math>\overline{p}(y)=p\left(Q^{-1}_{p}(y)\right)</math> 
on <math>X_{p}</math>, denote the corresponding [[Banach space]] as <math>\overline{X}_{p}</math> and let <math>i_{p}:X_p\hookrightarrow \overline{X}_p</math> be the natural embedding, then define the continuous map
:<math>\overline{Q}_p(x):=i_p\left(Q_{p}(x)\right)</math>
which is a map <math>\overline{Q}_p:X\to \overline{X}_p</math>. Let <math>q</math> be a seminorm such that for all <math>x\in X</math>
:<math>p(x)\leq C q(x),</math>
then define a continuous linear operator <math>T_{q,p}: \overline{X}_{q}\to \overline{X}_{p}</math> as follows:
* If <math>z\in i_q(X_q)\subseteq \overline{X}_q</math> then <math>T_{q,p}(z):=\overline{Q}_p\left(\overline{Q}^{-1}_q(z)\right)</math>, which is well-defined.
* If <math>z\not\in i_q(X_q)</math> and <math>z\in \overline{X}_q</math>, then there exists a sequence <math>(z_n)_n\in i_q(X_q)</math> which converges against <math>z</math> and the sequence <math>\left(T_{q,p}(z_n)\right)_n</math> converges in <math>\overline{X}_p</math> therefore <math>T_{q,p}(z):=\lim\limits_{n\to \infty}\left(T_{q,p}(z_n)\right)_n.</math><ref name="SmoFom">{{cite journal |first1=Oleg Georgievich |last1=Smolyanov |first2=Sergei Vasilyevich |last2=Fomin |author-link2=Sergei Fomin |title=Measures on linear topological spaces |journal=Russian Mathematical Surveys |volume=31 |number=4 |date=1976 |pages=26-27 }}</ref>

If <math>p</math> it ''Hilbertian'' then <math>\overline{X}_p</math> is a [[Hilbert space]].

===Sazonov topology===
Let <math>\mathcal{P}</math> be a family of continuous Hilbert seminorms defined as follows: <math>p\in \mathcal{P}</math> if and only if there exists a Hilbert seminorm <math>q</math> such that for all <math>x\in X</math>
:<math>p(x)\leq C q(x)</math>
for some constant <math>C\in \mathbb{R}</math> and if <math>T_{q,p}</math> is a [[Hilbert-Schmidt operator]]. Then the topology <math>\tau^S:=\tau^S(X,\tau)</math> induced by the family <math>\mathcal{P}</math> is called the '''Sazonov topology''' or '''S-topology'''.<ref name="SmoFom" /> Clearly it depends on the underlying topology <math>\tau</math>. If <math>(X,\tau)</math> is a [[nuclear space|nuclear]] then <math>\tau^S=\tau</math>.

===Statement of the theorem===
Let <math>\mu</math> be a cylindrical measure on <math>\mathfrak{A}</math> and <math>\tau</math> a locally convex topology that is compatible with the dual pair and let <math>\tau^S:=\tau^S(X,\tau)</math> be the Sazonov topology. Then <math>\mu</math> is σ-additive on <math>\mathfrak{A}</math> if the [[Fourier transform]] <math>\hat{\mu}(f):X'\to \mathbb{C}</math> is continuous in zero in <math>\tau^S</math>.<ref name="SmoFom" />
